messages:
Sophia: Hey team — invoice INV-9382 from Vertex Cloud got auto-flagged for a sales-tax exemption claim. vendor attached a ‘Resale Certificate - CA’ PDF but I can't find it on the vendor record. link: https://invoices.redwood/INV-9382
Alejandra: I don't see the cert in NetSuite either. Vendor portal shows an upload but it's an image, not the signed form we need. Can we ask them to re-send a signed PDF?
Raj: Quick q — do we have economic nexus in CA for this service? If we don't have nexus, we shouldn't be collecting CA sales tax from them, but the exemption still needs to be valid. @tim any tax/legal nuance for SaaS vs infra credits? :thinking_face:
Tim: Generally CA taxes some digital goods/services but resale certificates typically apply to buyers reselling tangible personal property. Need to confirm nature of the supply. If vendor is a reseller and they provided a valid CA resale cert in our name, that could justify zero tax. Send me the uploaded image and I'll review.
Sophia: Pasted invoice snippet below:
```
Invoice: INV-9382
Date: 2025-11-06
Vendor: Vertex Cloud LLC (US)
Line items:
 - Dedicated GPU hours x 120 = $3,200.00
Tax: $0.00 (exempt per vendor note)
Total: $3,200.00
Reference: 'Resale cert on file'
```
Alejandra: I've put a manual hold on this payment while we confirm docs. invoices-bot applied the hold.
invoices-bot: Payment hold applied to INV-9382 by @alejandra — reason: tax-exemption verification required — hold_until: 2025-11-20.
Raj: Thanks. If vendor can't produce a valid resale certificate that names Redwood or acceptable blanket certificate, we should treat tax as due. Do we have a playbook for requesting CA BOE-compliant certificates?
Alejandra: We do — legacy checklist in Confluence: /finance/tax/resale-cert-checklist. I'll ping vendor with a template asking for: 1) signed PDF, 2) purchaser name exactly 'Redwood Inference, Inc.', 3) state field filled, 4) effective date.
Sophia: Also need to know whether we should gross-up the invoice if vendor requests net amounts. Vendor asked if we can gross-up to cover potential tax — what's the policy?
Maria: @sophia per AP escalation: we do not gross-up automatically. If vendor requests gross-up, sales & legal approval needed and we prefer to re-invoice once tax status confirmed. I'll step in if vendor escalates.
Tim: If the vendor is claiming exemption incorrectly and tax is later assessed, we can try to recover from vendor but it's messy. Better to get the doc now or hold payment.
Alejandra: I'll send the request now and attach the CA resale certificate template.
Alejandra: Message to vendor (copied): "Hi — thanks for the invoice. Can you re-upload a signed PDF of your CA resale certificate naming 'Redwood Inference, Inc.' as purchaser? If you cannot, please confirm whether you expect Redwood to gross-up the invoice to cover any CA sales tax — note our AP team will not auto-gross-up without approval"
Sophia: Thanks. I'll drop the uploaded image here for @tim to review in case it's borderline.
Tim: Uploaded file looks like a consumer-facing image, missing seller info and signature. Not acceptable. We should hold. :no_good:
Raj: Noted. If vendor supplies a valid certificate within the hold window, AP will release payment. If not, escalate to @maria for decision on whether to withhold tax or return invoice for reissue.
Alejandra: Will follow-up in 48 hours and update this thread. cc @sophia @raj
Sophia: ACK. Marking thread for AP queue. :white_check_mark:
